title: Ban Zhao (Han historian)
summary: Ban Zhao was a scholar of the Later Han dynasty, daughter of the historian Ban Biao and sister of Ban Gu. After Ban Gu died in 92 CE she was called to the imperial library to complete the Book of Han, notably its eight tables, and wrote Lessons for Women, an influential treatise on female conduct.

uncertainty.note: Birth c. 45 CE and death c. 116-120 CE are approximate; sources give c. 45-120 (World History Connected) and ca. 45-116 (UCLA Center for Chinese Studies).

as_recorded.value: Ban Zhao (c. 45–120) was the first woman historian of China.

where.historical_name: Luoyang, capital of the Later Han dynasty (the capital, in the sources)

importance.justification: Completed the Book of Han and wrote Lessons for Women, shaping Chinese historiography and ideas about women's education and conduct.
